title: Extreme value theorem and attainment
section: Theorems Concerning Continuous Functions ▷ Extreme value theorem
terms: extreme value theorem; absolute maximum; absolute minimum; attainment; closed bounded interval.

exposition.text:
If f : [a, b] → R is continuous and a ≤ b, then it attains both an absolute maximum and an
absolute minimum. Thus there are c, d ∈ [a, b] with f(c) ≤ f(x) ≤ f(d) for all x in the interval.
The hypotheses combine continuity with compactness: a closed bounded interval supplies both
endpoints and prevents escape to infinity.
Attainment is stronger than boundedness. For example, a function may have finite supremum
on an open interval without taking that value. The theorem locates no particular maximizer
and guarantees no uniqueness. In calculations, examine endpoints as well as interior critical
points; for a continuous function whose minimum is strictly positive, taking reciprocals pre-
serves continuity and boundedness.

question.text:
If f is continuous and strictly positive on [0, 1], which statement must hold?
(A) f is increasing.
(B) inf f = 0.
[0,1]
(C) There is M > 0 such that 1/f(x) ≤ M for every x.
(D) f has exactly one minimum point.
′
(E) f is bounded.

solution.text:
The minimum is attained at some c. Since every value is positive, m = f(c) > 0, and
1/f(x) ≤ 1/m. Positivity without compactness would not ensure this uniform bound.

question.text:
Which continuous function has a finite supremum on its stated domain but no maximum?
2
(A) f(x) = x on [−1, 1]
(B) f(x) = x/(1 + x) on [0, ∞)
(C) f(x) = 1/x on (0, 1]
(D) f(x) = sin x on R
2
−x
(E) f(x) = e on R

solution.text:
For x ≥ 0, x/(1 + x) < 1 and tends to 1, so its supremum is 1 without attainment. Choice C
is unbounded above; A, D, and E attain their maxima.

question.text:
A continuous f : R → R satisfies f (x) → ∞ as |x| → ∞. Which must hold?
(A) f attains a global minimum
(B) f has only finitely many critical points
(C) f attains a global maximum
(D) f is one-to-one
(E) f has a zero

solution.text:
Outside a sufficiently large compact interval, f(x) > f(0) + 1. The minimum on that interval
exists by the extreme value theorem and is consequently a global minimum.

question.text:

(A) Neither is finite (B) 0, 1/4 (C) −1, 1/4 (D) 0, 1 (E) 1/4, 1/4

solution.text:
2
The expression is 1/4 − (x − 1/2) . Its supremum 1/4 is attained at 1/2; its infimum 0 is ap-
proached at the excluded endpoints.

question.text:
Which hypothesis guarantees that a continuous real function on a nonempty subset S ⊂ R
attains both extrema?
(A) S is connected
(B) S is bounded
(C) S contains infinitely many points
(D) S is closed
(E) S is closed and bounded

solution.text:
Closed and bounded subsets of R are compact, so the extreme value theorem applies.
Bounded open intervals and closed unbounded sets show why either property alone is
insufficient.
